findings.F1: The tested measure lies on the side opposite to the idea at every horizon from 2 to 10 days, not only at the plan's 5 days: forecast-weighted excess return t = -2.50 at 2 days (n=2579), -1.04 at 3 days (n=1735), -1.91 at 5 days (n=1067) and -2.67 at 10 days (n=505). On the positive-forecast cases, the mean excess 5-day return is -0.83% (t -2.57).
findings.F2: The thin-volume down days that do not rebound sit mostly in falling markets and in the early years, and they are not graded by the forecast.
findings.F3: The rebound the brief gives to thin-volume falls appears instead after heavy-volume falls, over about 3 days.
findings.F4: This heavy-volume rebound is strongest in the heaviest-volume falls.
findings.F5: The heavy-volume 3-day rebound is uneven across years and coins, though positive in most.
findings.F6: On the up side, heavy-volume moves carry on as the brief says, but only weakly.

ideas.idea: When a coin falls sharply over one day on volume well above its own 30-day average daily volume, it wins back part of that fall over the next 3 days; the larger the fall and the heavier its volume against that average, the larger the rebound.
ideas.consequence: A sharp drop on heavy volume marks capitulation selling that is absorbed within days, so it is a reason to buy the drop rather than sell it.
ideas.name: heavy-volume drop rebounds

ideas.idea: When a coin rises sharply over one day on volume well above its own 30-day average daily volume, it keeps rising over the next 5 days; the larger the rise and the heavier its volume against that average, the larger the further gain.
ideas.consequence: A sharp rise on heavy volume reflects spreading demand that continues, so it is a reason to hold or add to a long rather than fade it.
ideas.name: heavy-volume rise continues
